definitions.explanation: The flat green parts of a plant.

examples.japanese: {木|き}の{葉|は}が{赤|あか}く{色|いろ}づいてきた。
examples.english: The tree leaves have started turning red.

examples.japanese: {春|はる}になると{新|あたら}しい{葉|は}がたくさん{出|で}てくる。
examples.english: When spring comes, lots of new leaves appear.

examples.japanese: {秋|あき}になると{庭|にわ}の{木|き}の{葉|は}が{全部|ぜんぶ}{落|お}ちて、{毎日|まいにち}{掃除|そうじ}が{大変|たいへん}だ。
examples.english: In autumn, all the leaves on the trees in the garden fall, and cleaning up every day is hard work.

examples.japanese: {夏|なつ}の{間|あいだ}は{葉|は}が{茂|しげ}っていて{日陰|ひかげ}ができるので、この{木|き}の{下|した}で{休|やす}むのが{好|す}きだ。
examples.english: In summer the leaves are lush and create shade, so I like to rest under this tree.

notes:
{葉|は} means leaf or leaves, a basic nature vocabulary word.

READINGS:
- は: standalone or in some compounds
- ば: in certain compounds ({落|お}ち{葉|ば}, {青葉|あおば})
- よう: on'yomi reading ({葉緑素|ようりょくそ})

SEASONAL TERMS:
- {新緑|しんりょく}: fresh green leaves (spring)
- {青葉|あおば}: green/verdant leaves (early summer)
- {紅葉|こうよう}/{紅葉|もみじ}: autumn leaves/foliage
- {落|お}ち{葉|ば}: fallen leaves
- {枯|か}れ{葉|は}: dead/withered leaves

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {葉書|はがき}: postcard (originally written on leaves)
- {言葉|ことば}: word, language
- {木|こ}の{葉|は}: tree leaves
- {葉|は}っぱ: leaf (casual/childish)

EXPRESSIONS:
- {葉|は}が{茂|しげ}る: leaves are lush
- {葉|は}が{散|ち}る: leaves fall/scatter

RELATED:
- {枝|えだ}: branch
- {根|ね}: root
- {幹|みき}: trunk
